# Pidgeon

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Teddy  <sub>[v1 c18 P6](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0006)</sub>

## Personality

Mr. Pidgeon is an ineffective, sarcastic, and remarkably lenient teacher who maintains terrible discipline in his classroom. He frequently ignores younger students while focusing on older pupils preparing for examinations, often spending his class time assisting Sukey Pullen. Despite being prone to using spiteful remarks and physical punishment on his students, he maintained no actual order. However, he showed emotional sensitivity during his farewell address to his school, weeping alongside his pupils.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c19 P32](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0032), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_

## History

Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school. During his time as teacher, he maintained poor discipline, permitting pupils to play with crickets and eat green apples during lessons, while heavily focusing his attention on older students like Sukey Pullen. He frequently visited Sukey in the evenings under the pretext of aiding her schoolwork and bestowed Mayflowers upon her during a school outing. He embarrassed Nell Harcourt by holding up her marked slate to criticize her spelling, mocking her geometry skills, and disciplining her by forcing her to stand before the blackboard. Despite public criticism of his teaching, he retained his position because his uncle controlled the school trustees. Upon his departure from the school, he delivered an emotional farewell speech beginning with 'The time has come for us to part,' bringing both himself and his pupils to tears.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)_
